Agastya.description: A sage, son of Pulastya; met Rama during exile and gifted divine weapons.
Agastya.notes: Uncle of Ravana through lineage; important teacher figure.

Ahalya.description: Wife of sage Gautama; cursed for infidelity and later liberated by Rama.
Ahalya.notes: Her liberation by Rama is a notable episode.

Akampana.description: Maternal uncle of Ravana; instigated Ravana to abduct Sita; killed in battle by Hanuman.
Akampana.notes: Portrayed as one of the instigators of war.

Akshayakumara.description: Youngest son of Ravana and Mandodari; killed by Hanuman in Ashoka Vatika encounter.

Angada.description: Son of Vali and Tara; aided Rama in the search for Sita and fought against Ravana's forces.

Añjanā.description: Mother of Hanuman; often described as a vanara princess or apsara incarnation.

Atikaya.description: Son of Ravana and Dhanyamalini; mighty warrior killed by Lakshmana with a Brahmastra.

Bharata.description: Second son of Dasharatha (born to Kaikeyi), younger half-brother of Rama; ruled Ayodhya as regent in Rama's name.
Bharata.notes: Key figure demonstrating loyalty and dharma.

Chandrabhaga.description: Wife of Kushadhvaja; mother of Mandavi and Shrutakirti (wives of Rama's brothers).

Dasharatha.description: King of Ayodhya and father of Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna; died broken-hearted after Rama's exile.
Dasharatha.notes: Central royal figure whose boons and promises drive the exile plot.

Devantaka.description: A son of Ravana; described as a warrior killed by Hanuman.

Dhanyamalini.description: Second wife of Ravana; mother of Atikaya.

Dhumraksha.description: One of Sumali's sons; maternal uncle of Ravana; killed by Hanuman.

Dushana.description: Twin brother of Khara; a demon of Dandaka forest killed by Rama.

Ganga.description: River goddess often referenced in epics; included in Ramayana narratives as sacred river.
Ganga.notes: Appears in many Hindu epics and lore; contextual in Ramayana episodes.

Guha.description: King of Śṛṅgiverapura (Nishada); helped Rama cross the river during exile.

Hanuman.description: Divine vanara, devoted servant of Rama; central hero in Sundara Kanda and Ramayana overall.
Hanuman.notes: Often regarded as an avatar/incarnation associated with Shiva; key for Lanka mission.

Hema.description: An apsara mentioned in certain versions; mother of Mandodari in some accounts.

Indrajit.description: Elder son of Ravana (also called Meghanada); famed as a powerful warrior and wielder of illusion and celestial weapons.
Indrajit.notes: Killed in the war; important antagonist on Ravana's side.

Jambavan.description: King of the bears created by Brahma to assist Rama; wise elder of the vanara forces.
Jambavan.notes: Prominent in vanara council and search for Sita.

Janaka.description: King of Mithila; father of Sita; famed for wisdom and for the svayamvara of Sita.

Jambumali.description: One of Prahasta's sons; killed by Hanuman during the Ashoka Vatika episodes.

Jatayu.description: Vulture-demigod who tried to rescue Sita from Ravana and was mortally wounded; a noble figure.
Jatayu.notes: His attempt provides early clue to Sita's abduction location.

Kabandha.description: A cursed gandharva turned monstrous demon; freed by Rama and Lakshmana after his defeat.
Kabandha.notes: His story precedes alliances with Sugriva and Hanuman.

Kaikasi.description: Wife of Vishrava; mother of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, and Shurpanakha.

Kaikeyi.description: One of Dasharatha's queens and mother of Bharata; invoked boons that led to Rama's exile.
Kaikeyi.notes: Her action is pivotal to the exile plot.

Kausalya.description: Chief consort of Dasharatha and mother of Rama.

Khara.description: Brother of Dushana and cousin of Ravana; leader of rakshasa band defeated by Rama and Lakshmana.

Kumbhakarna.description: Brother of Ravana known for gigantic size and long sleeps; a mighty warrior killed in war.
Kumbhakarna.notes: Tragic figure often noted for his boon of long sleep.

Kusha.description: Son of Rama and Sita (twin of Lava); one of the youths to whom Valmiki taught the Ramayana.

Lakshmana.description: Younger brother and constant companion of Rama; guarded Rama and Sita during exile; twin of Shatrughna.

Lava.description: Son of Rama and Sita (twin of Kusha); associated with later retellings and founding legends.

Lankini.description: Female guardian of Lanka's gates; personification of the city in some accounts.

Malyavan.description: An elder rakshasa and one of Sumali's sons; opposed Ravana's abduction in some versions.

Mandavi.description: Daughter of Kushadhvaja; cousin of Sita; wife of Bharata.

Mandodari.description: Chief consort of Ravana; described as pious and righteous in many accounts; mother of Indrajit.

Manthara.description: Maid of Kaikeyi who persuaded her to demand boons that caused Rama's exile.
Manthara.notes: Often depicted as the manipulative catalyst of exile.

Maricha.description: Demon who assumed the form of a golden deer used to lure Sita; involved in abduction plot.

Nala.description: Vanara credited with constructing Rama Setu (bridge) along with his twin Nila.
Nala.notes: Son of Vishvakarma in some versions.

Narantaka.description: Son of Ravana; killed by Angada in battle.

Nila.description: Commander-in-chief of the vanara army; twin of Nala and credited in Rama Setu construction.

Nirvani.description: A yakshini mentioned as niece of a yaksha king in some lists.

Parashurama.description: The sixth avatar of Vishnu; confronts Rama over Shiva's bow and later accepts Rama's identity as Vishnu's incarnation.
Parashurama.notes: Important for validating Rama's divinity in some episodes.

Prahasta.description: Maternal uncle of Ravana and chief commander of Lanka's army.

Rama.description: Protagonist of the epic; avatar of Vishnu; son of King Dasharatha; epitome of dharma and virtue.
Rama.notes: Central deity-hero; principal figure for fact-check answers about Rama in scripture context.

Ravana.description: King of Lanka; main antagonist who abducted Sita; son of Vishrava and Kaikashi.
Ravana.notes: Complex character with devotion to Shiva and scholarly aspects.

Rishyasringa.description: A sage who presided over a sacrifice enabling Dasharatha to beget sons; married to Shanta in some versions.

Rumā.description: Wife of Sugriva; her abduction by Vali justifies Rama's slaying of Vali in some accounts.

Sampati.description: Brother of Jatayu; helped trace Sita with divine vision and informed Rama of her location.

Shanta.description: Daughter of Dasharatha; adopted later by King Romapada; married to Rishyasringa in some accounts.

Shabari.description: An elderly ascetic devotee of Rama who offered him berries and guidance during the exile.

Shatrughna.description: Youngest son of Dasharatha and twin brother of Lakshmana; devoted to family duties.

Shiva.description: One of the Trimurti; appears in Ramayana context as a major god; associated with Hanuman in certain traditions.
Shiva.notes: Appears across Hindu epics; not exclusive to Ramayana.

Shrutakirti.description: Daughter of Kushadhvaja and Chandrabhaga; married to Shatrughna; cousin of Sita.

Shurpanakha.description: Sister of Ravana who desired Rama and attacked Sita; her humiliation by Lakshmana escalated the conflict.
Shurpanakha.notes: Her episode triggers subsequent events leading to Sita's abduction.

Sita.description: Principal female figure; wife of Rama; considered an incarnation of Lakshmi and famed for virtue.
Sita.notes: Central female protagonist; primary scripture source for Sita-related facts.

Subahu.description: A demon who harassed sages; killed by Rama as part of early exploits.

Sugriva.description: Vanara ruler of Kishkindha; ally of Rama; helped organize the vanara army against Lanka.
Sugriva.notes: Key ally whose conflict with Vali ties into the plot.

Suketu.description: A yaksha who performed a yajna and got a daughter named Tataka in some lists.

Sumali.description: Father of many rakshasa chiefs; progenitor of several Lanka nobles including Prahasta and others.

Sumantra.description: Prime minister of Ayodhya; trusted advisor to King Dasharatha.

Sumitra.description: Second consort of Dasharatha; mother of Lakshmana and Shatrughna.

Sunayana.description: Queen of Mithila; wife of King Janaka and mother of Sita and Urmila.

Tara.description: Wife of Vali and mother of Angada; renowned for wisdom and counsel.
Tara.notes: One of the panchakanyas in later tradition.

Tataka.description: A woman transformed into a demon; slain early by Rama as part of his exploits.

Trijata.description: A demoness who guarded Sita during captivity; sometimes described as compassionate toward Sita.

Trishira.description: Son of Ravana; killed in battle (various accounts).

Urmila.description: Younger sister of Sita; wife of Lakshmana who remained at home during exile.
Urmila.notes: Known for sacrifice of sleeping for 14 years in some tellings.

Vali.description: Elder brother of Sugriva; great strength and king of Kishkindha; killed by Rama.
Vali.notes: Controversial episode involving Rama's slaying of Vali.

Vasishtha.description: Royal sage and spiritual advisor to Dasharatha and Ayodhya's rulers.

Vibhishana.description: Younger brother of Ravana who joined Rama's side and was later crowned king of Lanka.
Vibhishana.notes: Represents righteous dissent among Ravana's kin.

Vidyutjiva.description: A danava mentioned as husband of Ravana's sister in some lists.

Vishrava.description: Father of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana and Shurpanakha; son of Pulastya.

Vishvamitra.description: A sage who once was a king; guided Rama and Lakshmana early on and taught them duties and warfare.
Vishvamitra.notes: Instrumental in Rama's early exploits and lifting Shiva's bow.
